execution_overview.overall_summary: The agent executed both approved active candidates for Hendricks_QuartJournEco_2018_wNKW_path04 inside Docker. Task1 estimated an adjusted Huber robust linear model and Task2 estimated an unadjusted Huber robust linear model. Both found positive no-high-school versus college-degree log wage-gain coefficients, supporting the focal claim with statistically strong evidence.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The agent followed the planned Task1 path: it used the authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx dataset, constructed log wage gain and education groups, retained the planned controls, and estimated the planned Huber robust linear regression. No implementation repairs were needed.

other.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference='college_degree')) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob

result_raw.result_text: In the adjusted Huber robust model, immigrants with no high school had higher log wage gains than immigrants with a college degree. The focal coefficient was 0.280 log units, corresponding to an approximate 32.3% higher wage gain.

conclusion.rule_applied: Support requires the no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree to be positive. For frequentist coefficient-based results, p < 0.05 indicates strong support when the direction aligns; p >= 0.05 would indicate weak directional support. Opposite would require affirmative evidence of a negative contrary effect.
conclusion.uncertainty_statement: The estimate is positive and statistically significant at p = 0.000535, with an approximate 95% confidence interval excluding zero in the positive direction, indicating strong statistical support.
conclusion.conclusion_text: Task1 supports the focal claim because the estimated no-high-school wage-gain coefficient relative to college degree is positive and statistically significant.
